passage:
Tina wanted to try a new restaurant because it had hundreds of five-star reviews online. Her brother noticed something odd. Many reviews used almost the same words and were posted on the same day.
They checked other sites and found more mixed opinions. Some customers liked the restaurant, but many complained about slow service.
Tina still went, but she no longer expected perfection. The food was good, and the service was indeed slow.
She learned that reviews are useful, but they are not pure truth. Numbers can be shaped, bought, or repeated.
A smart reader does not only count stars. A smart reader asks who wrote them, when, and why.

本文沒有陳述「The New Classmate's Lunch」；這個選項混入另一個情境的資訊。
本文沒有陳述「The Quiet Bell」；這個選項混入另一個情境的資訊。
本文沒有陳述「The Special Pencil」；這個選項混入另一個情境的資訊。
